scope: Browser behaviour and pixels: the same deterministic gaussian-splat scene rendered twice per engine in one Playwright browser context - reference = real three.js + upstream @sparkjsdev/spark 2.3.1 (read-only port-repo bundles), target = this repo bundle through cc.CocosSparkLayer/cc.CocosRenderer/cc.sparkRuntime - with byte-exact RGBA8 read-back comparison. Scenes are procedural only (no .spz/.ply fixtures).
strictRule: Every RGBA8 channel byte difference must be 0; both images non-empty; each side stable against its own repeat; zero JS errors and zero drained GL errors; identical context attributes and unmasked renderer inside one engine; source/asset digest unchanged; negative control must move pixels. No tolerance.
claimLimit: Evidence is per-engine on THIS machine only (see results[].gpu). Nothing here generalises to other GPUs, drivers, devices or browsers not listed; no "works everywhere" claim is made. The reference adopts the target native float32 camera/mesh matrices and viewport, so this evidence covers the splat rasterisation/sort/blend path, while camera-matrix construction is covered by SPK-04 math parity.
